hints: Use $x=1$, $y=2$ to determine the constant, then exponentiate and isolate $y$.
walkthrough:
Integrate both sides with respect to their variables:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \dfrac{x + 2}{x + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Rewrite the integrand on the right-hand side using algebraic division:
$$\dfrac{x + 2}{x + 1} = \dfrac{(x + 1) + 1}{x + 1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{x + 1}$$

Evaluate the right-hand integral term by term:
$$\int \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = x + \ln(x + 1)$$

Write down the general solution with constant of integration $c$:
$$\ln y = x + \ln(x + 1) + c$$

Substitute the initial condition $x = 1$ and $y = 2$ to find $c$:
$$\ln 2 = 1 + \ln(1 + 1) + c \implies \ln 2 = 1 + \ln 2 + c \implies c = -1$$

State the equation with the evaluated constant:
$$\ln y = x + \ln(x + 1) - 1$$

Exponentiate both sides to express $y$ explicitly in terms of $x$:
$$y = \mathrm{e}^{x + \ln(x + 1) - 1} = \mathrm{e}^{\ln(x + 1)} \cdot \mathrm{e}^{x - 1} = (x + 1)\mathrm{e}^{x - 1}$$
